clue.text: Dock below expanse of land?

parts.note: sub- is the Latin prefix for under or beneath
a tract is a large stretch of country

explanation.surface: A question about what lies beneath a stretch of land, as if a dock sat under it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a noun for a harbour, but here it is the verb meaning to deduct, as in docking someone's wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock pay is to take an amount off it, a synonym of deducting.

clue.text: Tear visible in small lithograph?

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a lithograph is one kind of print, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone spots a rip in a little lithograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as a rip in the paper, but it is the verb for racing along, rhyming with 'care'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to run at full speed, a short fast dash.

clue.text: Exercises a lot of contrition, having throttled popular bird

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise

indicators.note: to throttle is to squeeze round the neck, so the shortened word grips the next piece inside it
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: contrition is sorrow or regret for a wrong
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Physical jerks and much remorse somehow strangle a well-liked bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' leaves REGRE, and 'having throttled' makes that grip the word for popular, giving REGRINE after the exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine is a falcon, a bird of prey famed for its diving speed.

clue.text: Early religious leader favoured by the monarch

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A churchman of the early days enjoys royal favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter, chief of the apostles, is regarded as the first leader of the Christian church.

clue.text: Reversing finished, posh car's engine's sound

indicators.note: the word for finished is turned backwards, as a car might reverse

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in time is up
RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car

explanation.surface: When a smart car backs out after its trip, its engine makes a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth engine idling is said to purr, the low contented hum of a cat.

clue.text: Wretched fellows going to a town in Ireland

parts.note: bally is a dated British euphemism for bloody, so wretched or damned
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Miserable chaps head off to an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLY is an old-fashioned British mild swear word standing in for 'bloody'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballymena is a market town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Names in USA misrepresented as MS PA?

definitions.note: a personal assistant who handles manuscripts, a person taking dictation

indicators.note: shown wrongly, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: American names are wrongly shown as if they were abbreviations for a woman and a state.
explanation.walkthrough: MS and PA look like Mississippi and Pennsylvania, or Ms and a dad, but read as manuscript plus personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a literary assistant who writes from dictation or copies manuscripts.

clue.text: Possibly arm foremost of members in political party, in short

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

indicators.note: the foremost letter is the first one of the following word

explanation.surface: Perhaps a wing of a party starts with its members.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is one example of a bodily limb, hence the 'Possibly'.

clue.text: Regiment's first to penetrate enemy front

indicators.note: the single letter pushes into the enemy word like an attacking force

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: the first letter of the regiment's name is taken

explanation.surface: A regiment is the first to break through the enemy's front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Fore means the front part, as in the fore of a ship.

clue.text: Bicycle with screw loose nearly going around as he collapsed

indicators.note: the shortened word surrounds the next piece
almost all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: someone with a screw loose is mad, bonkers

indicators.note: fallen down in a heap, so the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bike with a loose screw nearly turns over as its rider falls off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with screw loose' means crazy, so the bicycle is not the thing with a loose screw. 'nearly' leaves BONKER; 'collapsed' jumbles the two short words, and 'going around' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneshaker was the nickname for early bicycles with rigid frames and iron tyres that jolted the rider.

clue.text: Recalled most of working party turned up undernourished

indicators.note: called back, so everything that follows is read backwards
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a detail is a small group of soldiers given a special task
came means arrived or turned up

explanation.surface: A work squad was summoned back, though most of it arrived half-starved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims DETAIL to DETAI; with CAME added this gives DETAICAME, which 'Recalled' reads backwards. 'turned up' looks like the reversal signal, but it is CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated describes someone abnormally thin from lack of food, starved.

clue.text: Ace cracking second iron strongbox

indicators.note: breaking into, so the single letter goes inside the pair that follows

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: An expert breaks into a strongbox in a second with an iron bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' suggests an expert safecracker, but it gives the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe is a strong, lockable box for valuables.

clue.text: Keen to gamble, choosing other member of bridge team

indicators.text: choosing other member of bridge team
indicators.note: bridge partners are North-South and East-West, so West is swapped for East

parts.note: to wager is to bet or gamble

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to bet and picks a different partner at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players sit as North, South, East and West; West's partner is East, so W gives way to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and eager are synonyms, both meaning enthusiastic.

clue.text: Rained freely, swamping spot in water conduit

indicators.note: flooding over, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
loosely, without restraint, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or dominoes

explanation.surface: It poured so hard that a pipe carrying water flooded a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges the first word into DRAINE, which 'swamping' wraps around the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainpipe is a pipe carrying rainwater from a roof, so a conduit for water.

clue.text: Hear about the ultimate in fashion

indicators.note: around, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
the end is the ultimate or final point

explanation.surface: Listen to the latest word in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like listening, but it is the court sense: to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means stylish and up to date, exactly what is in fashion.

clue.text: One fools eleven in Berlin without considering others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
nits are nitwits, fools
elf is German for eleven

explanation.surface: One team of eleven fools in Berlin, ignoring everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing taken in itself is considered alone, apart from everything around it.

clue.text: Idiots succeed in exam, switching two components

indicators.note: two letters of the word trade places, the first and the third

parts.note: to pass is to succeed in an exam

explanation.surface: Fools manage to pass a test by swapping a couple of parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching two components' swaps the P and the first S of PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saps are gullible fools, a slang word for idiots.

clue.text: Source of disappearance: large, marine but mysterious?

definitions.text: Source of disappearance: large, marine but mysterious?

indicators.note: puzzling, so the letters are shuffled
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cause of vanishings that is big, at sea and baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' gives D, the first letter of 'disappearance'; 'mysterious' shuffles D with LARGE MARINE BUT. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This stretch of the western Atlantic is famed in legend for ships and planes vanishing without trace.

clue.text: Fixed equipment like blotting paper, not soft

parts.note: a rig is apparatus or equipment, as in a drilling rig

indicators.note: the letter for soft is left out of the word before it

parts.note: blotting paper soaks up ink, so it is porous
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Kit that absorbs like blotting paper is fixed so it is no longer soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorous means strict and unbending, so fixed and not open to change.

clue.text: 17 Celsius tops scale

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the answer to 17 across, an arm or a leg

explanation.surface: Seventeen degrees Celsius is the highest reading on the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' points to the answer of 17 across, which supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or a mountain is to go up it.

clue.text: Fruit tree father planted around a yard initially

indicators.note: set in place surrounding something, so these pieces enclose the next letter

parts.note: papa is a word for father

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Dad has put a fruit tree in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives Y from 'yard', and 'planted around' puts PAPA and A round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya is a tropical tree bearing large, sweet, orange-fleshed fruit.

clue.text: Imprisoned regularly, I'm free at last at the critical moment

parts.note: in the nick is British slang for in prison
oft means often, regularly

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A prisoner, locked up regularly, is finally free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an every-other-letter signal, but it is OFT. 'Nick' is British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something just before it is too late is an idiom for arriving at the last possible moment.

clue.text: Study drinking venue in article with little substance

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
to read a subject is to study it at university
a bar is a place for drinking

explanation.surface: Studying in a pub, as described in an article, has little substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A threadbare argument is thin and weak, like cloth worn through.

clue.text: Energy completely visible in current? That's what you experience

indicators.note: seen inside something, so the pieces sit within the word for current

parts.note: rife means widespread, current
E is the physics symbol for energy
all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: Energy fully on show in an electric current is something you feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests electricity, but here it means prevalent, as in rumours being rife.
explanation.definitionFit: Actual lived experience, as opposed to fiction or theory, is what happens to you.

clue.text: Regulator intended to get rid of a perplexity

parts.note: a baffle is a plate that regulates the flow of air, sound or liquid

indicators.note: the word sheds the following letter

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A control device was meant to clear up confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflement is a state of being puzzled, confusion.

clue.text: No upturn in work on magazine, maybe: number twelve

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: to edit is the work done on a magazine, for one

explanation.surface: No sign of an upturn for magazine work: the issue is number twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn' reads the editing word and the number from the bottom up, making ONTIDE. 'number twelve' looks like the definition, but 'number' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is an old word for midday, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Casket enthusiast will identify wood

parts.note: a casket is a chest or box
a nut is a fan, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A fan of boxes can tell which wood one is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut timber comes from the chestnut tree, a hardwood used for furniture.

clue.text: The setter is brought in by new staff for hunter

indicators.note: the setter's phrase goes inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
the setter refers to himself, so with 'is' it means I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler gets taken on by a new team as a hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick, ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod, the mighty hunter of Genesis, is a byword for a keen huntsman.

clue.text: Medic bristles, looking haggard

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor
an awn is the bristly tip on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A doctor bristles with anger and looks worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bristles' reads as a verb for bridling, but it is the botanical noun AWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks tired and strained, gaunt from worry or illness.

clue.text: Page abandoned unfinished when penning article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the shortened word surrounds the next letter
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: left means abandoned
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A page was left incomplete while an article was being written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts LEFT to LEF, and 'when penning' puts A inside it. 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is a single sheet of a book, two pages back to back.
